data.title: Scammers Drain $73,000 From Chase Account After Posing As Bank Fraud Investigators
data.description:
A grocery store worker says scammers posing as Chase Bank fraud investigators drained $73,000 from his savings.

The Mariano’s employee, identified as David Lipsky, transferred the money after callers claimed the FBI would arrest him if he did not move his funds into what they called a safe account, reports ABC7 Chicago.

Lipsky says the first call appeared to come from Chase and warned that his account had been compromised.

Says Lipsky,

“They worked with the FBI, they said. If I didn’t do it, they were going to get the FBI at my house and arrest me.”

He first tried sending $1,000 through Zelle, but Chase blocked that transfer, so the scammers told him to complete three branch transfers totaling $73,000.

When he later called the real bank, he was told the money could not be recovered.

“I can’t afford this. I’m a frontline worker. I don’t make a hundred thousand dollars a year. I make an average salary. I need that money back.”

About $24,000 was later returned to his account, but he is still seeking the rest and says he needs it to keep paying his mortgage.

Palatine police obtained nationwide arrest warrants charging Jose A. Luis Mateo, 35, Fredduar A. Escobar Bautista, 28, and Breider A. Iriarte Campomar, 35, with theft by deception.

Chase says these scams are heartbreaking, that the blame lies with the perpetrators, and that the bank recovered some of Lipsky’s funds and will keep working with law enforcement.

Anyone with information can tip Palatine police at 847-359-9000.

Experts say hang up on unexpected bank fraud calls and contact your bank only through a number you look up yourself.

data.title: Texas Man Pleads Guilty to $15,000,000 Bank Fraud Using Fake IDs
data.description:
Federal prosecutors have secured a guilty plea from a Texas man accused of depositing more than $15 million in fraudulent U.S. Treasury checks through fake accounts and stolen identities.

Kendrick Lamont Fugett, 34, of West Dallas admitted to the charges on September 17th, 2026, before Chief U.S. District Court Judge Reed O’Connor in the Northern District of Texas, says the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Northern District of Texas.

He posed as a chief financial officer to open accounts at multiple banks, including one in Dallas where he deposited a $13.8 million Treasury refund check using a fake Texas driver’s license and fraudulent corporate documents.

In another instance, Fugett used a fake Illinois driver’s license to deposit a $447,000 refund check at a Bank of America branch in Mesquite while impersonating a company chairman.

Says U.S. Attorney Ryan Raybould,

“Mr. Fugett’s guilty plea reflects our office’s commitment to protecting federal funds. We will continue to work closely with our law enforcement partners to hold accountable those who steal from the American taxpayer and Main Street Americans.”

Fugett was arrested on August 20th and faces a maximum of 30 years in prison, with sentencing set for January 14th, 2027.

IRS Criminal Investigation led the case, which is being prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorneys Ignacio Perez de la Cruz and Alexander Schwab.

data.title: Amway To Hand $225,000,000 After FTC Alleges Deceptive MLM Recruitment
data.description:
A major multilevel marketing company has agreed to pay hundreds of millions of dollars to settle federal claims it misled recruits about earnings and pressured them into buying products they were unlikely to sell.

The proposed settlement requires Amway Corp., World Wide Group and Leadership Team Development to pay $225 million, nearly all of it for consumer redress, according to the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) and the state of Washington.

The complaint alleges the companies falsely promised income above $40,000 a year or a path to replace a full-time job, when most independent business owners who joined after 2020 spent more on products and training than they earned.

It also claims the firms told participants to falsify sales reports to hide a model built more on recruitment than real product sales.

The order adds new rules, including a requirement that independent business owners resell at least 70% of monthly purchases, lower pay for recruiters whose downline fails to move inventory, prompt sales reporting with customer receipts, independent audits, and a ban on first-year training fees from approved providers.

Says Christopher Mufarrige, Director of the FTC’s Bureau of Consumer Protection,

“Amway and its affiliates misled prospective workers with false earnings claims and then pressured them to buy Amway products they were unlikely to be able to sell. Today’s action makes clear that the FTC will not tolerate any company deceiving workers—whether through deceptive earnings claims or by promoting reports of false sales to make direct selling or multilevel marketing opportunities look appealing to consumers.”

data.title: New York Couple Drains $150,000 From Elderly Man’s Bank Account and Coin Collection: Report
data.description:
A New York couple has drained more than $150,000 from an elderly Delaware man by repeatedly tapping his bank account and pawning coins taken from his safe deposit boxes.

Bonnie Stiner, 56, and Craig Stiner, 55, of Belmont, New York, each received two years in prison plus probation on August 31st of 2026 after pleading guilty to felony theft and conspiracy in the second degree, reports Eastern Shore Undercover.

The theft stretched from January of 2022 to March of 2023, while the victim was 92 years old. He has since died.

Over that stretch, the Stiners accessed the man’s bank account dozens of times and spent the cash on bills, vacations and entertainment.

Craig Stiner also drove the victim to his bank, pulled hundreds of valuable coins from the man’s safe deposit boxes, and pawned them with his wife.

Delaware Attorney General Kathy Jennings blasted the scheme.

“Theft in any capacity is criminal, to steal an entire life’s savings from a nonagenarian is utterly despicable. While nothing can undo the harm that was caused to the victim, I am proud that these offenders will serve their time in prison, and thankful for our DOJ team and our partners in the Wilmington Police Department who helped bring them to justice and secure restitution for the victim’s family.”

The Stiners must pay restitution to the victim’s family during probation. Delaware DOJ’s Economic Crimes Unit handled the case.

data.title: Visa and Mastercard Paying $167,500,000 To Settle ATM Surcharge Lawsuit – Here’s the Deadline for Submitting a Claim
data.description:
Visa and Mastercard are paying $167.5 million to settle claims they blocked independent ATMs from offering lower fees.

ClassAction.org reports the deal covers U.S. consumers who paid unreimbursed surcharges at non-bank ATMs from October 24th of 2007 through August 14th of 2026.

The lawsuit said the networks’ rules stopped independent ATM operators from discounting access fees when a cheaper competing network could process the withdrawal, pushing cardholders to pay more.

According to the settlement administrator’s portal, Visa and Mastercard prevented independent automated teller machine from discounting or charging cardholders “a lower access fee if transactions could be processed on competing networks that cost less than the Visa or Mastercard networks.” Subsequently, consumers paid higher access fees to use independent ATMs than they would otherwise have.

Under the settlement, Visa is handing out $88,775,000 while Mastercard will pay $78,725,000. After fees and costs, valid claimants share the fund pro rata.

A federal judge in the District of Columbia granted preliminary approval on August 14th of 2026. Claims are open through February 10th of 2027 on the settlement administrator’s portal, NonbankATMSurchargeSettlement.com, and a final approval hearing is set for February 17th of 2027.

Despite agreeing to the settlement, Visa and Mastercard deny any wrongdoing.

A related ATM surcharge lawsuit against the two payment card networks settled for $197.5 million in 2024, as previously reported. In that lawsuit, Visa and Mastercard were accused of conspiring with major banks to prevent independent ATM operators in the US from charging lower fees.

data.title: Bank Insider Responsible for Stopping Fraud Steals $1,000,000+ From Elderly Customers Aged Between 90 to 103: Report
data.description:
A former bank employee hired to stop financial crime has been sentenced to 10 years in prison for stealing more than $1 million from elderly customers.

The sentence was handed down in federal court in Cleveland and covers roughly that loss figure after prosecutors had cited about $2 million at trial, reports Cleveland.com.

U.S. District Court Judge Philip Calabrese sentenced Yue Cao, 36, to eight years on 10 counts of bank fraud and one count of money laundering, plus two years for four counts of identity theft.

Cao worked at KeyBank from 2015 to 2022 as a quant analytics manager building models meant to prevent financial crimes.

He used an offshore service to create fake email addresses, enrolled more than 100 victims in online banking without their knowledge and moved money into accounts he controlled.

Victims lived in Ohio, New York, Pennsylvania, Connecticut and Washington and ranged in age from 90 to 103, including a 103-year-old woman.

Prosecutors said Cao picked victims because of their age and because he believed they were unlikely to report the theft.

The scheme surfaced after suspicious transfers were flagged at Charles Schwab, where Cao later worked.

Judge Calabrese addressed how Cao got the information.

“He used his position of trust within financial institutions to gain access to personal information.”

Assistant U.S. Attorney Edward Brydle described how the theft unfolded.

“This was a slow, calculated process.”

Cao is a Chinese national and legal permanent resident who is expected to face deportation after his sentence.

The Daily Hodl previously covered his February conviction in this report.

data.title: New York Prosecutors Seek $61,000,000 Crypto Forfeiture From Iranian Military Oil Sales
data.description:
Federal prosecutors have filed a civil forfeiture complaint seeking approximately $61 million in cryptocurrency generated by black-market sales of sanctioned Iranian oil.

The proceeds were intended to finance Iran’s government and military components, including the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, a designated terrorist organization, says the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of New York.

Says Deputy U.S. Attorney Sean S. Buckley,

“The Government of Iran relies on black-market sales of sanctioned crude oil to fund its military and foster terrorism in the Middle East and around the world, along with other malign efforts to develop a nuclear program and ballistic missiles capable of delivering nuclear payloads.

As alleged in the complaint filed today, the Government of Iran used a network of cryptocurrency actors in China and elsewhere to launder more than $1.5 billion in illicit oil money intended to benefit the Iranian military and the terror-designated IRGC. Today we are seizing and seeking to forfeit more than $61 million of the Government of Iran’s money, which otherwise would have promoted hostile military action and terrorist attacks against the U.S. and our allies.”

Two Chinese firms known as Blessed Trust and Hexa Whale allegedly shifted oil proceeds through Binance accounts in the United Arab Emirates.

The companies also moved tens of millions of dollars through the U.S. financial system, the complaint alleges.

Those claims remain unproven until a court awards a judgment in favor of the United States.

The FBI New York Counterintelligence and Espionage Division handled the investigation.

data.title: Billionaire Stanley Druckenmiller Abruptly Dumps $61,000,000 of AI Infrastructure Asset, Boosts Stake In Amazon by More Than 1,000%
data.description:
Billionaire Stanley Druckenmiller has abruptly sold about $61 million of exposure to artificial intelligence infrastructure while lifting his Amazon stake by more than 1,000%.

New filings show Druckenmiller’s Duquesne Family Office exited all 195,955 Broadcom shares (AVGO) in the second quarter and added 495,800 Amazon (AMZN) shares.

Broadcom designs custom chips and networking gear that large technology firms use to train and run artificial intelligence systems.

The fund had opened that stake in the first quarter.

Meanwhile, the firm’s Amazon common-stock stake rose from 45,800 shares to 541,600 shares, an increase of 1,083%. That holding was valued at about $129 million at the end of June.

The same filing shows the office also sold out of Intel and Micron while adding a new Alphabet position of 336,300 shares.

Reported U.S. stock holdings rose to about $5.21 billion across 95 positions as of June 30th of 2026. The form was filed with the SEC on August 14th of 2026.

Duquesne Family Office is the New York firm that manages Druckenmiller’s public-equity book.
